source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Verify no error report during Mini DP driver installation and check the driver version is correct
1. Open the driver package and double click the executable file, the “InstallShield Wizard” will appear, and then click “Next”. In this example, “WinS2012.exe” is executed.
2. In the “Ready to Install the Program” screen, click “Install”.
3. After complete installation, click “Finish” and then reboot the machine.
4. Reboot the system after driver installation completes.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1.VGA can be installed without any problem.
2.VGA driver version is correct.
3.Digital Signer should be Microsoft Windows Hardware Compatibility Singed.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Driver: check the VGA driver is loaded (lspci shows VGA/display; the loaded drm/nouveau/ast module; recent drm/VGA dmesg lines). sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lspci | grep -i -E 'VGA|display' 2>&1; echo ---; lsmod | grep -iE 'drm|nouveau|ast' 2>&1; echo ---; dmesg | grep -i -E 'drm|VGA' | tail -n 15 2>&1"
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the VGA device + loader driver + DRM dmesg so the user confirms the VGA driver is present and initialized.

original_test_intent: Install the approved Windows MiniDP/VGA driver, verify error-free completion, exact driver version and Microsoft Windows Hardware Compatibility signer, reboot as approved and confirm the device remains healthy.
original_method: Launch the approved InstallShield executable, follow Next/Install/Finish, perform the required reboot sequence, then query Windows device/driver/signature state and review installer, Event Viewer and management logs.
manual_activity: No inherently human acceptance signal is specified. An authorized agent can drive the documented installer UI or an officially supported unattended mode, reboot, and collect exact Windows driver/signature evidence; an engineer supplies/approves the package and formal verdict.
required_inputs: Windows edition/build and VGA/MiniDP hardware IDs
Approved installer filename, hash, publisher, exact target version and compatibility record
Meaning of the required Microsoft Windows Hardware Compatibility signature
Approved reboot count, maintenance window, prior-driver backup and recovery credentials/path
safety_requirements: Do not run an unapproved or hash-mismatched executable.
Do not substitute a generic signed driver for the specified hardware-compatibility signer requirement.
Maintain KVM/OOB and a compatible rollback driver because install/reboot can remove display or boot access.
Stop on installer/signature/device/reboot failure, preserve the original failure and do not retry automatically.
agent_execution_scope: Verify package hash/signature and hardware/OS applicability before requesting the single plan approval.
Execute the approved unchanged installer/UI and reboot plan, capture full exit/UI timeline and reconnect once.
Collect Windows device status, exact driver version/provider/signer and Event Viewer/BMC/SEL evidence and compare Expected/Actual.
engineer_actions: Provide and approve the exact package, target version/signer, reboot semantics and rollback.
Ensure the independent KVM/OOB recovery path is available for the approved plan.
Review the automated evidence and issue PASS/FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Inapplicable to the source OS and coverage. Linux lspci/lsmod/dmesg only prove a Linux device/module state and cannot validate InstallShield, the Windows version, signer or reboot result.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the original approved Windows installer UI unless the exact vendor package documents an unattended switch; query Windows PnP/driver metadata and Authenticode/catalog signer using OS-native supported interfaces. Do not invent a silent switch.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: InstallShield Next/Install/Finish, both written reboot instructions pending clarification, version/signer criteria and 10/10-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Hash and signature-check the approved package, snapshot the current device/driver, execute the source GUI flow through controlled automation (or documented vendor silent mode), perform the owner-approved reboot count, then capture exact PnP status, version, provider, signer chain and relevant events.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact Windows build and VGA/MiniDP hardware IDs covered by the package.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record installer, driver, OS and firmware versions; do not infer compatibility.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Package vendor release notes/installation guide, Microsoft driver/signature metadata and owner approval.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds reproducible identity, rollback and evidence capture; it does not replace the approved installer or signature criterion.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction. Linux module evidence is removed as non-equivalent; GUI steps may be automated only through the same approved workflow.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Package, target, signer, reboot and rollback decisions.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An installer may change display availability or require a nonzero/reboot-required exit code; those meanings must come from its documentation.

project_override_considerations: A project supplies the package/version and may approve one reboot if it resolves the duplicate wording; completion must state the approved plan and cannot claim both source reboot steps were executed if only one was authorized. Package/approval inputs do not reduce automation capability or make the case permanently blocked.
expected_evidence: OS/hardware identity, pre-install driver state, approved package hash and signer
Installer UI/exit evidence and approved reboot timeline
Post-reboot exact driver version/provider/device status and Microsoft hardware-compatibility signer proof
Event Viewer/system/BMC/SEL health, rollback readiness, tool result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Steps 3 and 4 both require rebooting and may be duplicate rather than contradictory. The owner must clarify whether one or two reboots are intended, but the installation purpose remains clear.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The package and target facts are execution-readiness inputs. With them and one authorized unchanged plan, the complete core and evidence collection are automatable.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retain the idea that electronic validation is possible but replace its wrong-OS commands and missing installation coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retain its package/signature/recovery analysis, but reclassify to FULLY AUTOMATABLE because package provision and approval do not themselves make a technically automatable core PARTIAL.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates capability from readiness and engineer verdict while preserving the original Windows GUI method.

review_improvement: Corrects the Linux/Windows mismatch, preserves signer and installer coverage, and avoids downgrading capability merely because a driver package and approval are required.
independent_technical_reasoning: All acceptance facts—package identity, installer completion, version, device status, signer, reboot and logs—are electronically executable and collectable. The missing package and owner choices control readiness, not automation capability, so FULLY AUTOMATABLE is correct under V3.1.
